1.

Proceedings in the present matter arises by filing of Dar in Fir No.483/16 u/s 279/304-A Ipc of
Ps Madhu Vihar.

As per the facts the above mentioned case was registered on the statement of one
Sarvar who stated that on 05.09.2016 at about 10:00 am he along with his friend Himanshu Rajpoot
(since deceased) was traveling in bus bearing registration no.DL-1PD-0614 of orange colour route
no. 534 from Anand Vihar I.S.B.T. to West Vinod Nagar, Delhi.

The driver of the bus did not Mact
No.70/2017 Page 1 close the door of the bus.

When the bus reached near U-Turn, Flyover, he and his
friend Himanshu who were sitting in front seat of back window of the bus, the driver was driving the
bus in rash and negligent manner as a result deceased fell down from the bus.

Thereafter he
(complainant) along with the driver of the bus had taken Himanshu (injured) to Max hospital,
Patparganj where his Mlc got prepared.

He further stated that the driver of the bus was ran away
from the hospital.
2. Upon filing the Dar copy of the same was provided to respondents, consequently ld.

Predecessor
of this Tribunal by order dated 21.04.2017 proceeded respondent no. 2 ex parte.

In response to the
notice of Dar, respondent no. 1 and 3 appeared and filed their written statements.

3.

In the reply/written statement filed by respondent no.1, it is pleaded that accident did not take
place due to negligence of respondent no.1/driver.

It is further pleaded that the respondent no.1 was
the driver of the bus vide route no. 85 and as per Fir, the accident took place with the bus vide route

The driver was having valid driving licence and the vehicle in question was duly insured
with respondent no. 3.
4.
Reply to Dar was also filed by respondent no.3/insurance company wherein it is pleaded

that
alleged accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased and therefore
respondent/insurance company is not liable for compensation.

It is pleaded that in case respondent
no.1 and 2 (owner and driver of offending vehicle) do not contest the matter, respondent
no.3/insurance company is entitled to take all the pleas in terms of Section 170 of M.V. Act.

It is not
disputed that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.3 under policy
no.12140031160100000263.
5.

On the basis of pleadings following issues were framed on 21.04.2017:
Mact No.70/2017 Page 2
1. Whether Respondent no. 1 was driving vehicle bearing no. Dl-1Pd-0614 on 05.09.2016 at 10:30
am over U-turn, Anand Vihar Fly Over, Railway Line, Delhi in a high speed and in a rash and
negligent man- ner as a result its occupant namely Himanshu Rajpoot fell down from running bus
and sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries?

Opp
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for any com- pensation, if so, and for what amount ?

Opp
3. Relief.
6.
During the course of proceedings petitioners have examined three witnesses.

Pw1 is Raj Kishor
(father of the deceased), Pw2 is Sarvar Hussain who is complainant in the FIR/eye witness, Pw-3
Inspector Mousam Ghani, from Ps Bara Khamba Road, New Delhi.

On behalf of respondent no.1,
driver of the offending vehicle has appeared as R1W1.

No evidence has been led on behalf of
respondent no.3/insurance company.

7. I have heard Ms. Sulekha Thakur, ld. counsel for the petitioner and Sh.S. Ghosh, ld. counsel for
insurance company.

I have gone through the written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner as well
as insurance company.

My findings on the above framed issue is following:
Issue No.1
8.

On the aspect of rash and negligent driving, it is settled proposition of law that an action founded
on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is
sine qua non.

However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and
evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

Holistic view is to be
taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.

Strict rules of evidence are not

sentences.text: It is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner Ms.Sulekha Thakur that factum of deceased having died in road side accident is well proved by preponderance of probability.
However unfortunately post mortem of deceased could not be conducted.
However counsel for petitioner submits that for that reason, claim petition cannot be declined.

Counsel for the petitioner relied upon judgment of Hon'ble High Court in ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited vs.
Balvinder Kaur and others (MAC Appeal No.146/2012 decided on 10.11.2017).

sentences.text: It is further argued that on behalf of insurance a dispute has been raised with regard to bus being on route no.534 as mentioned in the FIR whereas the offending bus no. DL-1PD-0614 was not on that route.
It is argued that there is hardly any dispute with regard to involvement of the bus no. DL- 1PD-0614 as sufficient evidence has been led in this regard.
Counsel for the petitioner further submits that before the unfortunate death of deceased who was a young boy, parents spent Rs.1,62,000/- for medical expenses.
As they were not aware about the legal formalities, therefore after the death dead body was cremated without post mortem.

10. Sh.S. Ghosh, ld. counsel for insurance company submitted that without disputing the unfortunate death of the deceased, however liability upon insurance can be fastened only upon proof of involvement of vehicle MACT No.70/2017 Page 4 no. DL-1PD-0614 which was insured with respondent no.3.

It is further submitted that post mortem report of the deceased has also not been got conducted which caused doubt as to the veracity of the claim of petitioners as well as regarding the manner in which accident has taken place.

It is submitted that insurance company had taken a specific plea regarding sole negligence of the deceased resulting into his death and therefore petitioners were required to prove by preponderance of probability, not only the manner accident took place but also the fact that death has been caused due to accidental injuries.
According to counsel same has not been proved.
It is further argued that as per the complainant in FIR the bus on route no.534 caused the accident whereas as per PW R1W1 the offending vehicle was not on that route.
As such the offending vehicle has not been identified to be the one involved in the accident.
11. Having considered the submissions and going through the record.
PW1 Raj Kishor is father of the deceased, who admittedly was not the eye witness to the accident.
However deposition of PW1 is relevant to the extent that this witness stated that his deceased son was along with his friend namely Sarvar Hussain and were traveling in a bus.
Now for the purpose of deciding the issue under consideration, PW2 is the eye witness Sarvar Hussain who was stated to be accompanying the deceased at the time of accident.
As per PW2 on 05.09.2016 he and deceased were going to their home in East Vinod Nagar and took bus no. DL-1PD-0614.
PW2 states that deceased sat on the bus which was in front of the back gate of the bus.

PW2 states that when they reached Anand Vihar Flyover, driver of the bus who was driving it on a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly took a U-turn near railway line, Anand Vihar due to which deceased fell down from the bus and received fatal injuries.

PW2 MACT No.70/2017 Page 5 stated that accident Dar - Kusum Rani vs Subhash on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146312880/
3 occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bus no. DL-1PD-0614.
12.
It is matter of record that it is on the complaint of PW2, FIR No.483/2016 was registered.

In his statement given to the police for FIR, PW2 had not given the registration number of the bus and mentioned that bus on route no.534 was the one on which he along with deceased was traveling and accident occurred.
PW2 when cross examined by ld. counsel for the insurance company admits that he did not disclose the bus number initially as he was not aware about the same.
However it is matter of record that it is the bus no. DL-1PD-0614, whose driver was prosecuted in the above mentioned criminal case.
On the basis of facts emerging in the investigation, Investigating Officer served the notice u/s 133 M.V. Act.

In pursuance thereto respondent no.2/owner Anil Chandela undertook to produce the driver and thereupon it was admitted that bus no. DL-1PD- 0614 was involved in the accident and deceased died due to fall from that bus.
13.
It is important to note in this context that in the cross examination of PW2 nowhere it is suggested that bus no. DL-1PD-0614 was not involved in the accident.

Moreover beside evidence of PW2, Investigating Officer of FIR No.483/2016 was examined as PW3 Inspector Mousam Ghani who in his deposition has stated that on the basis of statement of the eye witness/complainant Sarvar, he served the notice u/s 133 M.V. Act to Depot Manager/respondent no.2, in pursuance thereto the offending vehicle along with driver was produced.
PW3 also stated that he recorded the statement of respondent no.2.

In cross examination of PW3 he admitted that during the investigation beside the statement dated 14.10.2016 of witness Sarvar and the response received to notice u/s 133 MACT No.70/2017 Page 6 M.V. Act, he had evidence in the shape of disclosure statement of driver, statement of the owner, to conclude that bus no. DL-1PD-0614 was involved in the accident.
14.

Thus having considered the evidence of PW2 and PW3 coupled with other material such as site plan, seizure memo of bus no. DL- 1PD-0614 and disclosure statement of respondent no.1, there is sufficient evidence available on the record.

In this context it is important also to refer the evidence of PW R1W1 who in his affidavit of examination in chief stated that he has been falsely implicated as he was driver of the bus on route no.85, whereas accident took place on route no.534.
However in cross examination PW R1W1 admitted regarding involvement of bus no. DL-1PD-0614 in the accident and being driven by him.
PW R1W1 also admitted that his bus was at Anand Vihar between 10.15 to 10.30 a.m. (around the time of accident).
PW R1W1 further admitted that he had never filed any complaint or representation regarding alleged false implication of him or bus no. DL-1PD-0614 to any authorities.

Thus, this Tribunal is of the considered view that deposition of PW2 and PW3 along with other documentary evidence establish accident having been caused by bus no.
DL-1PD-0614 due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 resulting into fall of the deceased and his death due to head injury in the accident.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioner.
Issue No.2 15.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and MACT No.70/2017 Page 7 reasonable.

As per Dar - Kusum Rani vs Subhash on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146312880/
4 settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

sentences.text: A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 16.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Himanshu Rajpoot.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121

Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017,
laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.

The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to Dar - Kusum Rani vs Subhash on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146312880/
5
the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the MACT No.70/2017 Page 9 legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

17. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Medical Expenses 18.
Petitioner has also made claim regarding medical expenses before death of the deceased.
In this regard PW1 in his evidence has referred to medical bills Ex.PW1/C which are stated to have been verified by the Investigating Officer and made part of the DAR.
As per Ex.PW1/C a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- was deposited in the hospital.
19. Ld. counsel for insurance company submits that first of all document Ex.PW1/C is a photocopy.
Moreover this document does not get support even from the fact that such amount has been reimbursed or not.

Ld. counsel for petitioner on the other hand submits that documents may be a photocopy but same has been duly verified by the Investigating Officer in the investigation itself and stamp of SHO of concerned Police Station is imprinted.

sentences.text: Having considered the submissions and evidence of PW1 along with documents Ex.PW1/C, first of all document Ex.PW1/C is part of DAR and that fact is not disputed.
Moreover nothing has come in the cross-examination of PW1 challenging the authenticity of above said documents.
As such this Tribunal finds that by preponderance of probability petitioner has proved on record that expenditure of MACT No.70/2017 Page 10 Rs.1,50,000/- has been done.
As such petitioner is entitled for claim of Rs.1,50,000/- under this head.

Age of deceased :
21.
Father of the deceased (PW1) in his evidence has proved copy of Aadhar card and educational certificates of deceased as Ex.PW1/B.
Perusal of document Ex.PW1/B shows that it is certificate of Secondary School Examination in the name of deceased Himanshu Rajput, according to which his date of birth is 30.06.1995.
This document in the opinion of this Tribunal is conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (05.09.2016) was around 21 years 02 months.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
22.
PW1 deposed that his son was doing private job and preparing for SSC Exams also and earning Rs. 20,000/- per month.
During cross- cross-examination PW1 admitted that he has not submitted any document to show the employment and income of his deceased son.
He also admitted that he has not filed any document to show that his deceased son was preparing for SSC Exams.
23. No documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioner to prove the employment and income of the deceased.
In the absence of any evidence and material either oral or documentary, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner has failed to prove that deceased was earning at the time of his death.

In the absence of any such material this Tribunal assesses income of deceased at parity with minimum wages of 'Matriculate but not Graduates' in the State of Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.11622/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
24.
As held above, deceased was about 21 years 02 months of age MACT No.70/2017 Page 11 at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:

MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs Dar - Kusum Rani vs Subhash on 15 January, 2024

7  M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5 Age group between 66 and above 25.
In view of the above, multiplier of 18 has to be applied against the age bracket of 21 to 25 years to determine the compensation.

Future Prospects:
26.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 MACT No.70/2017 Page 12 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component."
27.

Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 21 years 02 months, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
28.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th Dar - Kusum Rani vs Subhash on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146312880/
8 MACT No.70/2017 Page 13  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:

30. In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively
on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Therefore claimant i.e. mother of deceased is entitled to a sum of Rs.84,000/- (48,000 + 18,000+ 18,000) under this head.

INTEREST ON AWARD 33.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 34.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is matter of record that the vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
Therefore the amount of compensation is payable by respondent no.3/ insurance company to the petitioner.
Relief 35.

This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.19,91,246/- to the petitioner along with interest @
8% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by respondent no.3/insurance company.

Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal MACT No.70/2017 Page 15 during the pendency of this case.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the aspect of rash and negligent driving, it is settled proposition of law that an action founded
on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is
sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and
evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be
taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Thus, this Tribunal is of the considered view that deposition of PW2 and PW3 along with other documentary evidence establish accident having been caused by bus no.
DL-1PD-0614 due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 resulting into fall of the deceased and his death due to head injury in the accident.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 16.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Himanshu Rajpoot.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to Dar - Kusum Rani vs Subhash on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146312880/
5
the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
In the absence of any evidence and material either oral or documentary, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioner has failed to prove that deceased was earning at the time of his death.
In the absence of any such material this Tribunal assesses income of deceased at parity with minimum wages of 'Matriculate but not Graduates' in the State of Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.11622/- per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
27.
Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 21 years 02 months, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
